sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》旗下每日简讯《DealBook》的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼等众多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费阅读权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Jayon, do you remember the first time that you started thinking about the backlash in this country against Asian Americans in response to the coronavirus?
sentences.zh: 嘉阳，你还记得你第一次开始思考这个国家针对亚裔美国人的反弹，是在新冠疫情爆发之后的什么时候吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, around, I guess this is the beginning of March,
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，大概，我想这是在三月初,

sentences.en: I had seen on Instagram a friend and a fellow writer documenting an incident in Manhattan where I think he is Korean American and he was told by a stranger to, you know, get away.
sentences.zh: 我在 Instagram 上看到一个朋友兼同行作家记录了曼哈顿发生的一起事件，我想他是个韩裔美国人，一个陌生人叫他，你知道，走开。

sentences.en: But I remember reading about that incident and thinking, yeah, I mean, like, that's really terrible that this has happened.
sentences.zh: 但我记得读到那起事件时我想，是的，我的意思是，这发生得真糟糕。

sentences.en: But wondering, like, is this a singular incident or is there a trend?
sentences.zh: 但又在想，这只是一起孤立事件，还是说这是一种趋势？

sentences.en: As a journalist, and perhaps by my own personal temperament, I'm pretty cautious.
sentences.zh: 作为一名记者，也许也因为我个人的性格，我相当谨慎。

sentences.en: I don't like to make sensational generalizations that go well on a headline.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢做出那种适合上头条的耸人听闻的概括。

sentences.en: I feel like I need very convincing proof that something is happening before I call it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在下定论之前，我需要非常有说服力的证据证明某事正在发生。

sentences.en: And especially as a Chinese American, I wanted to make sure that I was not crying racism before I had the full evidence.
sentences.zh: 特别是作为一个华裔美国人，我想确保在掌握充分证据之前，我没有大喊种族歧视。

sentences.en: I wonder if it's because if I don't make too big a deal out of it, it won't be fully real.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这会不会是因为如果我不把它搞得太大惊小怪，它就不会那么真实。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I get to the gate at LAX.
sentences.zh: 我到了洛杉矶国际机场的登机口。

sentences.en: Home Depot.
sentences.zh: 家得宝。

sentences.en: In an Uber pool.
sentences.zh: 在一辆拼车里。

sentences.en: A grocery store, Wegmans.
sentences.zh: 一家杂货店，维格曼斯。

sentences.en: We were walking from the gym to get in our classrooMs.
sentences.zh: 我们正从健身房走去上课。

sentences.en: I got some milk, a little pasta.
sentences.zh: 我买了一些牛奶，一点意大利面。

sentences.en: Most of everything's gone.
sentences.zh: 大部分东西都卖光了。

sentences.en: And at that moment, there was this guy, looked like a regular guy.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，有这么个家伙，看起来像个普通人。

sentences.en: He was staring at me.
sentences.zh: 他一直在盯着我看。

sentences.en: As the death toll from the coronavirus rises in the U.S., so do reports of verbal and physical attacks against Asian Americans.
sentences.zh: 随着美国新冠肺炎死亡人数的上升，针对亚裔美国人的言语和肢体攻击报告也在增加。

sentences.en: And a couple of feet away from me, a man was seated and presumably his wife comes back to sit down and says out loud, You people, you brought it.
sentences.zh: 离我几英尺远的地方坐着一个男人，大概是他的妻子回来坐下后大声说，你们这些人，是你们带来的。

sentences.en: You're sick.
sentences.zh: 你们生病了。

sentences.en: Fuck China.
sentences.zh: 去你的中国。

sentences.en: China is stupid.
sentences.zh: 中国真愚蠢。

sentences.en: I ought to kill you.
sentences.zh: 我该杀了你。

sentences.en: I ought to shoot you.
sentences.zh: 我该枪毙你。

sentences.en: This girl looks Chinese.
sentences.zh: 这女孩看起来像中国人。

sentences.en: She must have the virus.
sentences.zh: 她肯定有病毒。

sentences.en: I can't sit next to her.
sentences.zh: 我不能坐在她旁边。

sentences.en: Who say that they are being blamed for the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 他们说自己被指责为这场大流行的罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: A person at the White House used the term Kung Flu.
sentences.zh: 白宫的一个人用了“功夫流感”这个词。

sentences.en: My question is, do you think that's wrong?
sentences.zh: 我的问题是，你认为这错了吗？

sentences.en: Kung Flu.
sentences.zh: 功夫流感。

sentences.en: And do you think using the term Chinese virus, that puts Asian Americans at risk, that people might target that?
sentences.zh: 你认为使用“中国病毒”这个词会把亚裔美国人置于危险之中吗？人们可能会针对他们？

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，一点也不。

sentences.en: I think they probably would agree with it 100%.
sentences.zh: 我想他们可能会百分之百地同意。

sentences.en: It comes from China.
sentences.zh: 它来自中国。

sentences.en: There's nothing not to agree with it.
sentences.zh: 没有什么不同意的。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Last question.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题。

sentences.en: You know, when the president asked, I don't think they would mind, you know, it being called the Chinese virus.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当总统问的时候，我不认为他们在意被叫做中国病毒。

sentences.en: I mind.
sentences.zh: 我在意。

sentences.en: It did make me feel different and kind of didn't really want to be Chinese because of the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 这确实让我感觉自己与众不同，因为新冠疫情，我甚至有点不想当中国人了。

sentences.en: Jiayang Fan, a writer for The New Yorker magazine, shares her story.
sentences.zh: 《纽约客》杂志撰稿人樊嘉阳分享了她的故事。

sentences.en: It's Friday, April 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月10日，星期五。

sentences.en: Jiayang, can you tell me a little bit about your childhood?
sentences.zh: 嘉阳，能跟我讲讲你的童年吗？

sentences.en: Where did you grow up?
sentences.zh: 你在哪里长大？

sentences.en: I was born in 1984 in Chongqing, China.
sentences.zh: 我1984年出生于中国重庆。

sentences.en: My mom was a doctor.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈是一名医生。

sentences.en: My dad was a researcher.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸是一名研究员。

sentences.en: And he was one of the first batch of scholars sent to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他是被派往美国的首批学者之一,

sentences.en: to bring Western knowledge technology and technology back to China.
sentences.zh: 把西方的知识技术和技术带回中国。

sentences.en: So he leaves when I'm about two.
sentences.zh: 所以我大概两岁时他就走了。

sentences.en: So I have very little memory of him.
sentences.zh: 所以我对他的记忆非常少。

sentences.en: But for my mom and I, life in China feels very serene and comfortable.
sentences.zh: 但对我妈妈和我来说，在中国的生活感觉非常宁静和舒适。

sentences.en: Whatever sense I have of the outside world, the world beyond China is very, very vague and
sentences.zh: 我对外部世界、对中国以外世界的任何概念都是非常非常模糊的,

sentences.en: incredibly hazy.
sentences.zh: 极其朦胧。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not quite sure it exists.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不太确定它是否存在。

sentences.en: But I think if one place were to stand out, it would be the United States.
sentences.zh: 但如果要说哪个地方最突出，那一定是美国。

sentences.en: I remember my mom and her friends talking about the show Dynasty, which did telegraph the glamour of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我记得我妈妈和她的朋友们谈论电视剧《豪门恩怨》，这部剧确实传达了美国的魅力。

sentences.en: I like that one.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那个。

sentences.en: It's a rather expensive fur.
sentences.zh: 这是一件相当昂贵的皮草。

sentences.en: I like the mink.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢水貂。

sentences.en: That is mink.
sentences.zh: 那是水貂。

sentences.en: The sense that this is what an everyday Joe would inhabit.
sentences.zh: 给人的感觉是，这就是一个普通美国人会居住的环境。

sentences.en: And this is, of course, a soap opera about an incredibly wealthy oil family living in a crazy, gorgeous home and driving along oil fields.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是一部肥皂剧，讲述了一个极其富有的小康家庭，住在疯狂、华丽的房子里，车子开过油田。

sentences.en: So it's actually quite exceptional.
sentences.zh: 所以它实际上非常非凡。

sentences.en: My name happens to be Mrs. Stephen Carrington.
sentences.zh: 我的名字正好叫史蒂芬·卡灵顿夫人。

sentences.en: I'm not used to haggling over what suits me or what it costs.
sentences.zh: 我不习惯为适合我的东西或它的价格讨价还价。

sentences.en: Well, it was the show.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就是这部剧。

sentences.en: And it was also at the time in China, what was very popular were these calendars of American
sentences.zh: 当时在中国也很流行那种美国

sentences.en: families where every member had golden hair, sparkling blue eyes and perfect bone structure.
sentences.zh: 家庭日历，上面每个成员都有金色的头发、湛蓝的眼睛和完美的骨相。

sentences.en: And they were always smiling with their perfect white teeth.
sentences.zh: 他们总是露着完美的白牙微笑着。

sentences.en: They always were sitting by a perfect colonial house or just out in nature.
sentences.zh: 他们总是坐在完美的殖民风格住宅旁，或者置身于大自然中。

sentences.en: But, you know, in front of a park that they look like they owned.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，站在一个看起来像是他们自己拥有的公园前面。

sentences.en: And I remember the food that really encapsulated America to me were Cheerios.
sentences.zh: 我记得真正让我体会到美国是什么的食物是谷物圈麦片。

sentences.en: Cheerios.
sentences.zh: 谷物圈麦片。

sentences.en: Yes, Cheerios.
sentences.zh: 是的，谷物圈麦片。

sentences.en: I had no idea what they tasted like.
sentences.zh: 我当时根本不知道它们是什么味道。

sentences.en: But the company did fantastic branding in China.
sentences.zh: 但这家公司在中国做了出色的品牌推广。

sentences.en: I remember the picture of the perfect baby on these ads for Cheerios.
sentences.zh: 我记得这些麦片广告上那个完美宝宝的照片。

sentences.en: You know, the round cheeks, the blue eyes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，圆圆的脸蛋，蓝色的眼睛。

sentences.en: That baby got to have this superior breakfast food that I, in all likelihood, would never get to taste.
sentences.zh: 那个婴儿能吃到这种极品早餐，而我按常理永远也尝不到。

sentences.en: So there's me, you know, drinking my Chinese porridge and, you know, eating my pickled vegetables
sentences.zh: 所以当时是我，在喝着我的中国粥，吃着我的咸菜,

sentences.en: and having fantasies about Cheerios, which I learned years later to not be very tasty at all.
sentences.zh: 幻想着谷物圈麦片，而我多年后才知道它们其实一点也不好吃。

sentences.en: They're actually kind of tasteless.
sentences.zh: 它们其实没什么味道。

sentences.en: To be like the definition of blandness.
sentences.zh: 简直就是平淡无奇的代名词。

sentences.en: But in your mind, they are this superior food for this kind of blonde haired, perfect group of people.
sentences.zh: 但在你心里，它们是这种金发碧眼、完美人群的顶级食物。

sentences.en: Yeah, for superior people, to put it bluntly.
sentences.zh: 是的，直白地说，是给优越的人吃的。

sentences.en: I mean, I still remember actually the first time I heard English.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我其实还记得我第一次听到英语。

sentences.en: I think it might have been my fifth or sixth birthday.
sentences.zh: 我想那可能是我五岁或六岁的生日。

sentences.en: And my mom might have come back pretty recently from English language training sessions.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈可能是不久前才从英语培训班回来。

sentences.en: And she just said the words, happy birthday.
sentences.zh: 她只是说了“生日快乐”这几个字。

sentences.en: That was, that was astounding to me.
sentences.zh: 那对我来说，太震撼了。

sentences.en: It was like my mom was superwoman.
sentences.zh: 感觉我妈妈就像个女超人。

sentences.en: That she knew how to say this language that did not sound like a language to me.
sentences.zh: 她竟然会说这种听起来一点也不像语言的语言。

sentences.en: Happy birthday.
sentences.zh: 生日快乐。

sentences.en: I still remember the way the syllables came out of her mouth and the image, which was of a tsunami.
sentences.zh: 我依然记得音节从她口中吐出的方式，那个意象就像是一场海啸。

sentences.en: There was this tidal wave of kind of one syllable consuming the next one.
sentences.zh: 有一种前一个音节吞没后一个音节的海啸。

sentences.en: And that to me was very incomprehensible.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说非常不可理解。

sentences.en: And I remember the time thinking, I will never learn this language.
sentences.zh: 我当时心想，我永远也学不会这门语言。

sentences.en: I have no hopes of ever learning this language, which is probably okay because I only need one language, right?
sentences.zh: 我根本不抱任何学会这门语言的希望，这可能也没关系，因为我只需要一种语言，对吧？

sentences.en: And it's Chinese.
sentences.zh: 那就是中文。

sentences.en: But essentially, something happens in the June of 89 that changes my father's fate as well as that of my mom and I forever.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，89年6月发生的一件事永远改变了我父亲以及我和我妈妈的命运。

sentences.en: The noise of gunfire rose from all over the center of Peking.
sentences.zh: 北京市中心到处都响起了枪声。

sentences.en: The Tiananmen Massacre.
sentences.zh: 天安门事件。

sentences.en: The mood of terror in the center of the city and quiet.
sentences.zh: 市中心弥漫着恐怖和寂静的气氛。

sentences.en: So the U.S.
sentences.zh: 于是美国

sentences.en: government immediately makes provisions for Chinese scholars who might need to flee from China.
sentences.zh: 政府立即为可能需要逃离中国的中国学者做出安排。

sentences.en: The demonstrators in Tiananmen Square.
sentences.zh: 天安门广场的示威者。

sentences.en: And that was when my mother and I joined my father in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 也就是那时，我和母亲去美国与父亲团聚。

sentences.en: Remember about first arriving in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 还记得刚到美国的时候。

sentences.en: We land in JFK and my father is living at the time in New Haven, Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 我们在肯尼迪机场降落，当时我父亲住在康涅狄格州纽黑文。

sentences.en: And that drive from JFK to New Haven, it is gray and drab-like tones that are not at all what I had imagined.
sentences.zh: 从肯尼迪机场到纽黑文的那段车程，是一片灰色和单调的色调，完全不是我想象的那样。

sentences.en: So I keep waiting for the real America to reveal itself to me.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在等待真正的美国向我展露它的真容。

sentences.en: So it is a rude awakening when my dad leads us to his second floor studio.
sentences.zh: 因此，当父亲带我们去他的二楼单间公寓时，这是一个残酷的现实打击。

sentences.en: There's just a mattress on the floor.
sentences.zh: 地板上只有一张床垫。

sentences.en: And I think it takes me a real, a good minute to realize that this is my new home.
sentences.zh: 我想我花了好长一段时间才意识到这就是我的新家。

sentences.en: And the loss of a language is pretty traumatic for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，失去一门语言是相当痛苦的经历。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: School started a few months later and I could not understand my teachers, my classmates.
sentences.zh: 几个月后开学了，我听不懂老师和同学的话。

sentences.en: And repeatedly, my new American teachers ask me, why aren't you talking more?
sentences.zh: 我的新美国老师反复问我，你为什么不多说说话？

sentences.en: Why aren't you engaging?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不积极参与？

sentences.en: And those expectations, I think, are hard for me to fully understand.
sentences.zh: 我想，这些期望对我来说很难完全理解。

sentences.en: And I feel like I'm walking blind into a game where I don't know the rules.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己像个盲人一样走进了一场我不知道规则的游戏。

sentences.en: I mean, not only do I not speak the language, I'm bringing pickled fish and rice.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不但不会说这门语言，还带着咸鱼和米饭。

sentences.en: And that's not sitting well with other kids at a lunch table.
sentences.zh: 这在午餐桌上的其他孩子看来很不合群。

sentences.en: All I feel is defeat.
sentences.zh: 我感受到的只有失败。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It sounds very lonely.
sentences.zh: 听起来很孤独。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Retrospectively, I think what made me feel most lonely was that I couldn't, I couldn't share those feelings with my mother.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，我觉得最让我感到孤独的是，我不能，我无法与母亲分享那些感受。

sentences.en: And I think for my mother, who worked very low-paying menial labor jobs in the U.S., a drastic step down from her position as a doctor in China,
sentences.zh: 我想对于我的母亲来说，她在美国从事着薪水极低、干粗活的体力工作，这与她在中国当医生的地位相比是一个巨大的落差,

sentences.en: she must have felt as marginalized and as embarrassed by her immigrant status as I do, but in an adult way, but similarly lacking in emotional vocabulary to express those feelings.
sentences.zh: 她一定和我一样，对自己的移民身份感到边缘化和尴尬，但她是带着成年人的方式，同样缺乏表达这些感受的情感词汇。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Like, I remember going to the mall for the first time with my mother, and my mom's favorite pastime was window shopping, just looking at things that she couldn't afford.
sentences.zh: 就像我记得第一次和母亲去商场，我妈妈最喜欢的消遣就是逛橱窗，只是看着她买不起的东西。

sentences.en: And I remember one time someone trying to hand her maybe a flyer for some store, and she said, no thanks.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次有人试图递给她一张某个商店的传单什么的，她说，不用了谢谢。

sentences.en: But she couldn't pronounce it correctly.
sentences.zh: 但她发音不准确。

sentences.en: So this young man said, no sex?
sentences.zh: 所以这个年轻人说，不要性吗？

sentences.en: Did you say no sex?
sentences.zh: 你刚才说没有性？

sentences.en: No sex?
sentences.zh: 没有性？

sentences.en: And I think I was like 11 or 12 at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且我当时大概11岁或12岁吧。

sentences.en: I remember that my mother actually just, in this embarrassed way, kind of laughed, like out of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我记得我母亲当时只是用那种尴尬的方式，笑了一下，就好像出于焦虑那样。

sentences.en: Like, she wanted it to be okay.
sentences.zh: 就好像，她希望这件事没什么。

sentences.en: She wanted to respond in a way to indicate that she was not offended.
sentences.zh: 她希望用一种能表现出她没有被冒犯的方式来回应。

sentences.en: But I remember the way that my cheek, just how hot and red they grew and how I felt so humiliated on my mother's behalf.
sentences.zh: 但我的脸颊发烫、变红的记忆依然历历在目，我为我的母亲感到无比屈辱。

sentences.en: And that experience feels seared into my brain, not just because of the insult, but because my mother had to swallow her own humiliation.
sentences.zh: 而且那种经历像烙印一样刻在我的脑海里，不仅仅是因为受到的侮辱，还因为我母亲不得不把自己的屈辱咽进肚子里。

sentences.en: Did you understand, given your age, that this was racism?
sentences.zh: 以你的年龄，你当时明白这就是种族歧视吗？

sentences.en: I mean, how did you process it in that moment?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在那一刻是怎么消化的？

sentences.en: I think I turned over the incident in my mind for a long time after that.
sentences.zh: 我想在那之后的很长一段时间里，我一直在脑海里反复琢磨这件事。

sentences.en: I don't think I would have coded it as racism.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我当时不会把它定义为种族歧视。

sentences.en: I think I almost only understood racism as something that white people inflicted on black people.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我几乎只把种族歧视理解为白人对黑人施加的东西。

sentences.en: I had no idea, or I had very little idea of how Asians fit into the landscape of race in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道，或者说我几乎不知道亚裔是如何融入美国种族格局的。

sentences.en: And I didn't know how to understand incidents in which you were not called a very specific racial slur.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道该如何理解那些你没有被当面叫出某种特定种族蔑称的事件。

sentences.en: Like that, no thanks, no sex.
sentences.zh: 就像那个，不用了，没有性。

sentences.en: Like...
sentences.zh: 就像……

sentences.en: What was that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: What was that, exactly?
sentences.zh: 那到底是什么？

sentences.en: I think as an 11-year-old, in my head, I didn't want to be different.
sentences.zh: 我觉得作为一个11岁的孩子，我心里是不想与众不同的。

sentences.en: I didn't want to be the one lashing out at others for being racist, because inevitably, that would make me seem even more different.
sentences.zh: 我不想成为那个指责别人种族歧视的人，因为无可避免地，那会让我显得更加与众不同。

sentences.en: And I think my mother, you know, my mother was the closest person in my life.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得我母亲，你知道的，我母亲是我生命中最亲近的人。

sentences.en: But if she had a religion, it would be survival.
sentences.zh: 但如果她有什么信仰的话，那就是生存。

sentences.en: I learned from my mother not to rock the boat, not to shake the existing system, to basically understand how the existing system works, and then to ascend it in some way,
sentences.zh: 我从我母亲身上学到的是不要惹事生非，不要动摇现有的体制，基本上就是去理解现有体制是如何运作的，然后以某种方式顺应它，

sentences.en: to climb the ladder.
sentences.zh: 往上爬。

sentences.en: As long as you fit in better, you will live a more comfortable life here, and that should be the goal.
sentences.zh: 只要你更好地融入，你在这里就会过上更舒适的生活，这应该就是目标。

sentences.en: And did things start to get a little bit better eventually?
sentences.zh: 那事情后来开始慢慢变好了吗？

sentences.en: I start speaking better English.
sentences.zh: 我开始说更好的英语了。

sentences.en: I start really enjoying and then falling in love with the English language, something that I thought would never happen.
sentences.zh: 我开始真正享受并进而爱上英语这门语言，这是我以前认为永远不会发生的事。

sentences.en: That's really important for me, I have to admit.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，这对我真的很重要。

sentences.en: When that language, English, came to feel like a part of my body, I have to say, that felt like a homecoming to me.
sentences.zh: 当英语这门语言开始感觉像是身体的一部分时，我不得不说，那让我有一种回家的感觉。

sentences.en: And how old are you at this point where you're starting to fall in love with the language?
sentences.zh: 那你开始爱上这门语言的时候多大？

sentences.en: I think around maybe 12 or 13, and I'll never forget the first time in sixth grade when I said the phrase, come on.
sentences.zh: 我想大概12岁或13岁吧，我永远不会忘记六年级时第一次说出“come on”这个短语的那次经历。

sentences.en: Like, this sounds silly, but it was only sixth grade when I could comfortably say, come on, to a schoolmate, and I felt very triumphant.
sentences.zh: 听起来可能很傻，但直到六年级我才能自如地对同学说“come on”，我当时感到非常有成就感。

sentences.en: As if to say, enough of that, come on.
sentences.zh: 就好像在说，差不多得了，走吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: When I could say that, I was so aware of myself saying it, and I was saying it the way that a normal American speaker would say it.
sentences.zh: 当我能说出这句话时，我对自己说这句话的意识非常强烈，而且我是以一个地道的美国说话者的方言说出来的。

sentences.en: And I'll never forget the sense of pride that coursed through me.
sentences.zh: 我永远不会忘记那种在体内流淌的自豪感。

sentences.en: And there was no one I could celebrate it with, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我找不到任何人来分享这份喜悦，对吧？

sentences.en: Because imagine if then I turned to the classmate who I said, come on with, and said, did you hear me?
sentences.zh: 因为想象一下，如果当时我转过身对那个我说“come on”的同学说，你听到我刚才说的了吗？

sentences.en: I just said, come on.
sentences.zh: 我刚才说了，come on。

sentences.en: And that would have totally defeated its purpose.
sentences.zh: 那就会彻底失去它的意义。

sentences.en: But I remember it because it felt like a real Americanism.
sentences.zh: 但我记住了，因为它感觉像是一个真正地道的美国习惯用语。

sentences.en: And it just rolled off my tongue.
sentences.zh: 而且它就那样顺畅地脱口而出。

sentences.en: So in that moment, you finally sort of feel like you belong.
sentences.zh: 所以在那一刻，你终于有了一种属于这里的感觉。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I still see myself predominantly as a visitor and that my existence is pretty probational on good behavior.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然主要把自己视为一个访客，我的存在很大程度上取决于我的表现是否良好。

sentences.en: And if I behave well, I will be able to minimize the number of times that I stick out as someone who doesn't belong.
sentences.zh: 如果我表现得好，我就能尽量减少自己作为异类而显得格格不入的次数。

sentences.en: But then I started to realize that's not exactly how it works.
sentences.zh: 但后来我开始意识到，事情并不是完全这样的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而且不需要输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》的订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Jae Young, I wonder if you can tell me about what happened to you recently.
sentences.zh: 所以杰英，我想请你跟我讲讲你最近发生的遭遇。

sentences.en: So this was in mid-March when there were rumors that New York City would be put under lockdown because of coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 那是3月中旬，当时有传言称纽约市因为新冠疫情将要封城。

sentences.en: And I wanted to make sure I had enough food in the house if I had to stay in for an indefinite period of time.
sentences.zh: 我想确保如果我不得不无限期闭门不出的话，家里有足够的食物。

sentences.en: And I was also really worried about my mother who has a neurodegenerative disease and lives in a nursing home close by.
sentences.zh: 而且我也非常担心我患有神经退行性疾病、住在附近疗养院的母亲。

sentences.en: I knew that I wouldn't be able to see her for a while, and I had several errands lined up.
sentences.zh: 我知道我有一段时间不能去看她了，我有一连串的杂事要办。

sentences.en: One was to take out the trash, one was to mail my rent check, and one was to go a few blocks away to my neighbor's house to pick up a sack of rice.
sentences.zh: 一件是倒垃圾，一件是寄房租支票，还有一件是去几个街区外的邻居家拿一袋大米。

sentences.en: It was around evening time, and I had just left my apartment building.
sentences.zh: 那是傍晚时分，我刚离开我住的公寓楼。

sentences.en: And I was on the phone talking to my mother's health aide in Chinese.
sentences.zh: 我正在用中文和母亲的医疗护理员通电话。

sentences.en: And as I was turning around after putting the trash in the trash bin, this is right in front of my apartment, I heard Chinese, Chinese, Chinese bitch, fucking Chinese.
sentences.zh: 当我把垃圾扔进垃圾桶转过身时，就在我的公寓正前方，我听到有人喊：中国人，中国人，中国婊子，他妈的中国人。

sentences.en: But, you know, I don't think I fully believed what I was hearing.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我当时觉得我不是太相信自己听到的话。

sentences.en: And when I made eye contact with him, he kept speaking, you know, you're fucking Chinese.
sentences.zh: 当我与他对视时，他还在继续说，你知道的，你这个他妈的中国人。

sentences.en: And I realized that I was comprehending what he was saying did not stop him.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我听懂了他说的话并没有让他停下来。

sentences.en: That was when, in my ear, my mom's aide kind of paused and said, Are you okay?
sentences.zh: 就在那时，电话那头我妈妈的护理员停顿了一下说，你还好吗？

sentences.en: Is something happening?
sentences.zh: 发生什么事了吗？

sentences.en: And I couldn't really speak.
sentences.zh: 我几乎说不出话来。

sentences.en: I found myself walking down the street.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己正沿着街道往前走。

sentences.en: I think I was still really set on, I need to get rice.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时还是铁了心要：我得去拿米。

sentences.en: But then I found it really hard to continue walking because my legs just felt leaden.
sentences.zh: 但随后我发现自己很难再继续走了，因为我的双腿感觉重得像铅一样。

sentences.en: Like, I really, really wanted to continue walking.
sentences.zh: 就好像，我真的、真的很想继续走下去。

sentences.en: It would have only been a 10-minute walk away for me to fetch that rice.
sentences.zh: 去拿那袋米对我来说本来只需要走10分钟的路程。

sentences.en: But I found myself coming to a halt.
sentences.zh: 但我发现自己停下了脚步。

sentences.en: And even, I thought, if I just kept talking on the phone with my aide.
sentences.zh: 甚至，我想过，如果我继续和护理员通电话的话。

sentences.en: But then I thought, I'm talking in Chinese.
sentences.zh: 但转念一想，我在说中文。

sentences.en: Like, who else am I going to offend?
sentences.zh: 难道我还想去冒犯谁吗？

sentences.en: And then I just got off the phone.
sentences.zh: 然后我就挂了电话。

sentences.en: And once I got off the phone, I felt even more scared because I was so aware of being alone.
sentences.zh: 一挂断电话，我感到更加害怕了，因为我清晰地意识到自己孤身一人。

sentences.en: So this is not embarrassment or even shame in this moment.
sentences.zh: 所以此刻感受到的不是尴尬，甚至也不是羞耻。

sentences.en: This is just terror.
sentences.zh: 这就是纯粹的恐惧。

sentences.en: This is a very real sense of fright that I'm not going to make it to my friend's house to get my sack of rice.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常真实、害怕自己无法走到朋友家去拿那袋米的惊恐。

sentences.en: We started this conversation with you saying that your instinct, and maybe it's because you're a journalist,
sentences.zh: 我们在对话刚开始时，你提到你的直觉——也许是因为你是一名记者，

sentences.en: maybe it's as an Asian American, maybe it's both, is to minimize these incidents and to be kind of slow to see them as part of a larger phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为你是一名美籍亚裔，也许两者兼而有之——是尽量将这些事件淡化，并且反应迟钝，不愿将其视作更大社会现象的一部分。

sentences.en: But it sounds like this was different for you.
sentences.zh: 但听起来这次对你来说有所不同。

sentences.en: Am I right to think that?
sentences.zh: 我这么认为对吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not the first time I've been called a Chinese bitch.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不是第一次被人骂作中国婊子了。

sentences.en: But what was different about this incident was that this man seemed to really mean it.
sentences.zh: 但这次事件的不同之处在于，这个人似乎是真心实意的。

sentences.en: And I wondered, I mean, in retrospect, right?
sentences.zh: 我在想，我的意思是，事后回想起来，对吧？

sentences.en: I wondered at the relationship between the sense of conviction in the man's voice,
sentences.zh: 我在想这名男子声音中的那种确信感之间的关系，

sentences.en: his certainty that he was in the right to point out my Chineseness and to call me a Chinese bitch.
sentences.zh: 他坚信自己有权指出我的中国血统并骂我中国婊子。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I think about the things that were going on in his day, like, did he lose his job earlier in the day because of this virus?
sentences.zh: 我想到了他那天遭遇的事情，比如，他是不是因为这场病毒在早些时候失去了工作？

sentences.en: I mean, does he work in the service industry?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他是从事服务行业的吗？

sentences.en: Does he have a loved one who has also become a prisoner in a nursing home or hospital?
sentences.zh: 他是否有亲人也变成了疗养院或医院里的阶下囚？

sentences.en: And I think about the way that all those anxieties and rage and sadness might have hardened into something, like an instrument, almost a weapon.
sentences.zh: 我想到了所有的这些焦虑、愤怒和悲伤，它们可能会凝固成某种东西，就像一件工具，几乎成了一把武器。

sentences.en: And I think about me being a surface onto which he could use that weapon and lash out.
sentences.zh: 我想到了我成了一个承载体，他可以利用这件武器发泄情绪。

sentences.en: And I think about the probational nature of my Chinese-American existence in a sense that in better times,
sentences.zh: 我想到了我的美籍亚裔身份所具有的权宜性质，也就是说，在更好的时期，

sentences.en: in normal times, there are certain stereotypes that are cast upon me when I walk down the street.
sentences.zh: 在正常时期，当我走在街上时，会有某些刻板印象加诸我身。

sentences.en: But in a moment of crisis, when it seems plausible that the country where I was born could be responsible
sentences.zh: 但在危机时刻，当人们觉得我出生的国家可能对这场前所未有的全球大流行负有责任时，

sentences.en: for an unprecedented pandemic, that I become a person of suspicion.
sentences.zh: 我便成了一个受人怀疑的人。

sentences.en: And I become someone who it's quite easy, perhaps, to kind of target all your ire and anxieties.
sentences.zh: 我成了一个可能很容易成为倾泻所有怒火和焦虑的目标的人。

sentences.en: And that maybe gave him temporary relief to be able to identify someone or something as the cause for his hurt and for his anxieties.
sentences.zh: 这或许让他得到了暂时的解脱，能够找到一个人或一件事来作为他受到的伤害和焦虑的替罪羊。

sentences.en: So what do you do?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么做？

sentences.en: So I go home, double lock my door, pull out my phone, and get on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 所以我就回家，双重反锁上门，掏出手机，登录推特。

sentences.en: Okay, yes.
sentences.zh: 好的，是的。

sentences.en: I describe what happened and I tweet.
sentences.zh: 我描述了发生的事情并发布了推文。

sentences.en: I wasn't offended.
sentences.zh: 我没有被冒犯。

sentences.en: I was afraid.
sentences.zh: 我很害怕。

sentences.en: I was worried he knew where I lived.
sentences.zh: 我担心他知道我住哪里。

sentences.en: For the longest time, I've been telling friends in China that although racism against Chinese exists in this country, that's not what I feel in a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间以来，我一直对中国的朋友说，尽管这个国家存在针对中国人的种族歧视，但在大流行期间，我并没有这种感觉。

sentences.en: I've never felt like this in my 27 years in this country.
sentences.zh: 在这片土地生活的27年里，我从未有过这种感觉。

sentences.en: I've never felt afraid to leave my home to take out the trash because of my face.
sentences.zh: 我从未因为自己的长相而害怕出门倒垃圾。

sentences.en: I want to believe what happened is anomalous and that we're living in extraordinary times and fear can deform us.
sentences.zh: 我愿意相信发生的一切只是个特例，我们正生活在一个非同寻常的时代，恐惧能扭曲我们的心智。

sentences.en: I wonder now if I should have taken his picture.
sentences.zh: 我现在甚至在想，我当时是不是应该拍下他的照片。

sentences.en: I wonder what your mother would make of this incident.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你母亲会如何看待这件事。

sentences.en: And I wonder what she would think of the fact that you decided to share what happened to you so publicly.
sentences.zh: 我想她会怎么看待你决定如此公开地分享你的遭遇这件事。

sentences.en: I think if I were to tell her about the experience, she might not fully understand the import of it.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我把这段经历告诉她，她可能无法完全理解其中的重大意义。

sentences.en: She would say, well, were you hurt?
sentences.zh: 她会说，好吧，你受伤了吗？

sentences.en: And I would say no.
sentences.zh: 我会说没有。

sentences.en: And she would say, well, did you lose anything?
sentences.zh: 她会说，好吧，你失去什么东西了吗？

sentences.en: And I would say no.
sentences.zh: 我会说没有。

sentences.en: And she would say, do you feel like this man is going to cut you down and kill you now?
sentences.zh: 她会说，你觉得这个人现在会来砍你并杀了你吗？

sentences.en: And I would say, you know, probably not.
sentences.zh: 我会说，你知道的，大概不会。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会。

sentences.en: And she would say, well, why are you even telling me this?
sentences.zh: 她会说，那你为什么要告诉我这些？

sentences.en: Like, what is the big deal here?
sentences.zh: 这有什么大不了的？

sentences.en: Or if I were to tell her that I was having this conversation with you, she would say, why make something out of nothing?
sentences.zh: 或者如果我告诉她我正在和你有这样的对话，她会说，为什么要小题大做？

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: She would say, why are you crying victim here?
sentences.zh: 她会说，你为什么要在那里装受害者？

sentences.en: Why are you making this into a bigger deal than it really is?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要把这事搞得比实际情况更严重？

sentences.en: Do you want this to be how you're remembered for being that woman who was the victim of a non-incident?
sentences.zh: 难道你想让别人记住你是因为当了一个非小事事件的受害女性吗？

sentences.en: And what would you say in this imaginary conversation with your mother?
sentences.zh: 在这场与母亲的假想对话中，你会说些什么？

sentences.en: I think I would try in English, because I think it would be hard for me to find the words in Chinese to explain the significance of it.
sentences.zh: 我想我会试着用英文说，因为我觉得很难用中文找到合适的词来解释它的重要性。

sentences.en: Not on my physical well-being.
sentences.zh: 这无关我的身体安康。

sentences.en: Help me understand what you mean.
sentences.zh: 帮我理解一下你的意思。

sentences.en: Because the longest, I mean, I think my mom and I both lived with this fiction that if we could be perfect versions of ourselves, for example,
sentences.zh: 因为长期以来，我的意思是，我觉得我和我妈妈都生活在一个虚幻的假象中，以为如果我们能成为完美的自己，举个例子，

sentences.en: if my mother could pronounce thanks the way that it's supposed to be pronounced.
sentences.zh: 如果我母亲能把“thanks”这个词发音成它本该有的样子。

sentences.en: And for me, if I could say, come on, naturally, that had always been the goal of our American existence, was to somehow bend ourselves to a shape that America could accept.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，如果我能自然地说出“come on”，这一直是我们美国生存的目标，就是以某种方式扭曲自己，变成美国能够接受的形状。

sentences.en: I never dared to believe that I could actually help to make America better.
sentences.zh: 我从不敢相信我实际上能为让美国变得更好出一份力。

sentences.en: That was something I never dared to think was possible.
sentences.zh: 那是我想都不敢想的事。

sentences.en: But in experiencing this, it made me rethink my role as an American and how even me, even someone who is probationary, that I was in some very,
sentences.zh: 但经历了这件事后，它让我重新思考了我作为美国人的角色，以及甚至连我，甚至是一个身份受动摇的人，如何在一种非常、

sentences.en: very small way contributing to this country.
sentences.zh: 非常微小的程度上为这个国家做出贡献。

sentences.en: By pointing out the ways that it's failing itself, making clear the way in which this country still makes me feel ashamed is possibly one way in which I could make it better.
sentences.zh: 指出它自身运转失灵的地方，坦承这个国家仍然让我感到羞耻的方式，可能是我让它变得更好的一种方式。

sentences.en: And also, that's the best version of America.
sentences.zh: 这也是美国最好的一面。

sentences.en: Like, in all the conceptions of America that exists in my head, I actually think this ability to call out the worst parts of America to itself, my freedom to do so,
sentences.zh: 可以说，在我脑海中对美国的所有构想里，我其实觉得这种能够直面并指出美国最丑陋一面的能力，我这样做的自由，

sentences.en: this feels to me the most miraculous part of America.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说是美国最不可思议的部分。

sentences.en: But I think all of that would be, frankly, a bit too abstract to my mother.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，坦白说，所有这些对我母亲来说可能都有点太抽象了。

sentences.en: I think her quest for survival has been so concrete and lived, you know,
sentences.zh: 我觉得她对生存的追求是那么具体、那么切实，你知道的，

sentences.en: I'll never be able to repay her for the way that her very concrete existence has paved the way for my more luxuriantly abstract one.
sentences.zh: 我永远无法回报她，因为她极其具体的生存方式为我更为奢侈的抽象生活铺平了道路。

sentences.en: But that maybe that's a boundary between us that I've been able to cross and that no matter how many ways I try to explain it, in what language, if she'll fully understand.
sentences.zh: 但也许这是我们之间的一道界限，而我已经能够跨越它，无论我尝试用多少种方法、用什么语言去解释，她是否能完全理解。

sentences.en: But I really needed to make sure that, for my own sake, I could know that this did happen, that this was not a figment of my imagination, or that, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我真的需要确保，为了我自己的心理安宁，我能知道这一切确实发生过，这并不是我虚构出来的，或者说，你知道的，

sentences.en: in an hour's time or in 12 hours' time, I would try to minimize it in my own mind.
sentences.zh: 在一个小时后或十二个小时后，我会在自己心里把这件事轻描淡写过去。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您百忙之中接受采访。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您百忙之中接受采访。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来这里。

sentences.en: I'm still sorry that you had the experience you had.
sentences.zh: 对于你经历过的事，我依然感到抱歉。

sentences.en: I am too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: But I'm sure it will be a small experience in what is hopefully a very long and a much bigger one of living in America and being American.
sentences.zh: 但我确信，在未来希望漫长且广阔的美国生活和成为美国人的历程中，这只是一段小插曲。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: Majority Leader.
sentences.zh: 多数党领袖。

sentences.en: Our nation continues to battle the coronavirus pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我们国家仍在与冠状病毒大流行作斗争。

sentences.en: More than 400,000 Americans have tested positive.
sentences.zh: 超过四十万名美国人检测呈阳性。

sentences.en: Nearly 15,000 have lost their lives.
sentences.zh: 近一万五千人失去了生命。

sentences.en: And important public health measures are creating an economic catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 重要的公共卫生措施正在引发经济灾难。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the Labor Department said that another 6.6 million Americans filed for unemployment benefits in the past week.
sentences.zh: 周四，劳工部表示，在过去一周里，又有六百六十万美国人申请了失业救济。

sentences.en: That means, Mr. President, more than 16 million Americans have lost their jobs in only the last three weeks.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，总统先生，仅在过去三周里，就有超过一千六百万美国人失去了工作。

sentences.en: A tragedy that is hard to even comprehend.
sentences.zh: 这是一场甚至难以想象的悲剧。

sentences.en: Economists now believe that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 经济学家现在认为，美国的

sentences.en: unemployment rate is the worst since the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 失业率是大萧条以来最糟糕的。

sentences.en: The latest figures put even deeper pressure on Congress to adopt a new round of economic relief for workers.
sentences.zh: 最新数据给国会施加了更沉重的压力，要求其为工人通过新一轮经济救助方案。

sentences.en: But on Thursday, that legislation hit a roadblock in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 但在周四，该立法在参议院遇到了阻碍。

sentences.en: Democrats want to double the size of the bill by adding hundreds of billions of dollars for hospitals and local governments, which are facing major financial shortfalls.
sentences.zh: 民主党人希望通过为面临严重资金缺口的大医院和地方政府增加数千亿美元拨款，来将法案规模扩大一倍。

sentences.en: We don't have to divide along the usual lines so soon after we came together for the country.
sentences.zh: 我们在为国家团结在一起之后，不必这么快就沿着寻常的路线分裂。

sentences.en: To my Democratic colleagues, please, please, do not block emergency aid you do not even oppose just because you want something more.
sentences.zh: 致我的民主党同僚们，求求你们，千万不要仅仅因为想要得到更多，就去阻挠那些你们甚至并不反对的紧急援助。

sentences.en: But Republicans, led by Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell, say that money can wait.
sentences.zh: 但以参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔为首的共和党人表示，这笔资金可以再等等。

sentences.en: Let's continue to work together with speed and bipartisanship.
sentences.zh: 让我们继续以高效和两党合作的精神携手共事。

sentences.en: We will get through this crisis together.
sentences.zh: 我们将携手度过这场危机。

sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 我们周一见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《电线切割机秀》中，我们将为假期招待客人做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的妙招。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是深度睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会晕厥过去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症吗，对食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢收听的任何平台上搜索《电线切割机秀》。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。
